reasoning: The core problem — whether stacked monitors' errors are correlated and whether independence holds — is already substantially studied. "Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute" (arXiv 2605.15377) does almost exactly the proposed setup: it computes the pairwise Pearson correlation among monitors' score vectors on backdoored APPS samples, studies error decorrelation across diverse monitors/prompts, and shows that low correlation (non-independence) directly governs ensemble catch rate, even noting that monitors from the same base/prompt share systematic error modes. "AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?" (arXiv 2510.11235) directly tackles the defense-in-depth independence assumption, showing perfectly correlated failures nullify layering. "Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors" (arXiv 2507.15886, NeurIPS 2025) combines monitors on APPS backdoors, and "Practical challenges of control monitoring" (2512.22154) explicitly flags that control-effectiveness math presupposes monitor-score independence and recommends copulas. The one genuinely under-explored residual is the proposal's explicit framing — directly comparing the empirical AND/OR joint catch rate against the independence-predicted rate as a quantified "optimism gap" — which the ensemble paper acknowledges as an open gap ("mechanism underlying complementarity remains unclear"), so the specific contribution is mostly covered with only a minor novel angle.

evidence.title: Ensemble Monitoring for AI Control: Diverse Signals Outweigh More Compute
evidence.summary: Measures pairwise Pearson correlation among monitors' score vectors on backdoored APPS samples; shows monitor error decorrelation (diversity) drives ensemble catch rate and that same-base/prompt monitors share systematic errors. Nearly identical setup to the proposal but does not explicitly compare empirical joint catch rate vs the independence prediction.

evidence.title: AI Alignment Strategies from a Risk Perspective: Independent Safety Mechanisms or Shared Failures?
evidence.summary: Directly analyzes the defense-in-depth independence assumption, showing that when failure probabilities of safety techniques are correlated, layering provides little/no additional protection — the conceptual question the proposal targets.

evidence.title: Combining Cost-Constrained Runtime Monitors for AI Safety
evidence.summary: NeurIPS 2025 paper combining multiple monitors on APPS backdoored-code detection to maximize recall under cost; establishes the combine-cheap-monitors-on-backdoors setting the proposal builds on.

evidence.title: Practical challenges of control monitoring in frontier AI deployments
evidence.summary: Explicitly notes control-effectiveness calculations presuppose independence of monitor scores and recommends fitting copulas to capture dependence — confirming the independence-assumption concern is already recognized in the literature.
